parts.label: a
parts.technique: Conservation of linear momentum / collision of particles
parts.reason: No statement in the given specification covers momentum, impulse, or collisions between particles (M6-M9 statements cover quantities/units, kinematics, forces/Newton's laws, moments only; no CLM/impulse statement exists). This concept is absent from the spec list entirely.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Impulse-momentum equation
parts.reason: Impulse and momentum are not mentioned in any of the M6-M9 statements provided; no statement covers this topic, so it is out of spec regardless of the arithmetic.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Moments of forces on a non-uniform rod, resolving vertically
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers moments in simple static contexts, including problems with non-uniform rods and particles; the resolution of forces vertically and taking moments fits this statement.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.technique: Modelling assumption - parcel as a particle
parts.reason: Part of the same moments problem covered by M9.1; discussing modelling assumptions (particle) is a natural extension of this statement's context.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.technique: Modelling assumption - plank as a rod
parts.reason: Similarly covered as part of the moments/modelling context of M9.1.

parts.label: i
parts.technique: suvat equations for vertical motion under gravity
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae for motion in a straight line, and M8.3 confirms use of constant g; setting up and solving simultaneous equations for two particles falling under gravity fits this.

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: suvat equations for vertical motion under gravity
parts.reason: Continuation of the same technique (M7.3) using the found T value to compute h; standard constant acceleration in a straight line.

parts.label: i

parts.reason: M8.4 covers equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces, requiring resolving in two directions with trigonometric ratios; this matches the setup with tension, force F and weight.

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces
parts.reason: Uses the same equilibrium equations from M8.4 to solve for mass m.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Speed-time graph sketching
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers interpreting/using graphs in kinematics for motion in a straight line, including sketching speed-time graphs.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Area under speed-time graph / suvat for constant acceleration
parts.reason: M7.2 (area under graph) and M7.3 (constant acceleration formulae) cover finding times/distances from motion graphs and equations.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Area under speed-time graph / suvat
parts.reason: Same as (b): uses trapezium/graph area methods covered by M7.2/M7.3.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Magnitude of a velocity vector
parts.reason: P10.2 covers calculating the magnitude of a vector; velocity given in vector form, finding speed is a direct application.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Position vector as function of time (constant velocity)
parts.reason: M7.3 extends constant acceleration/velocity formulae to 2D using vectors (r = r0 + vt); this is standard position vector kinematics.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Solving for time using position vector components
parts.reason: Uses the position vector expression from (b), equating components, a straightforward extension of M7.3/P10 vector kinematics.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Relative position/vector kinematics to find speed of interception
parts.reason: Builds on parts (b) and (c) using vector kinematics (position vectors, distance, constant speed) all covered by M7.3/P10.4; no vector equation-of-line intersection method needed (just distance/time), so it remains in the vector kinematics scope.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles (system equation)
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly covers connected particles (tow bar) with resolving forces along the line of motion; M8.2 covers Newton's second law in a straight line with resolving.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law applied to one connected particle to find tension
parts.reason: Same connected particles context of M8.4, finding internal tow-bar force via N2L on one vehicle.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles on an inclined plane
parts.reason: M8.4's guidance explicitly extends connected particle problems to cases where at least one particle moves on an inclined plane, matching this part exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces perpendicular to inclined plane (equilibrium)
parts.reason: M8.4 covers equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces including resolving on an inclined plane (per its guidance on inclined-plane resolution).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Coefficient of friction using F ≤ μR model in equilibrium/limiting friction
parts.reason: M8.6 explicitly covers the F ≤ μR friction model, coefficient of friction, and limiting friction/statics on a rough surface.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law with friction on inclined plane, then suvat for speed
parts.reason: Combines M8.2/M8.6 (equation of motion with friction, resolving on inclined plane) and M7.3 (suvat to find final speed) - all covered by the statements.
